statement: The system shall provide visual indicators on the MMI screens showing the range and position of each joint to inform the operator when approaching movement limits.
The system shall change the display color on the MMI screens when approaching or reaching joint movement limits.
The system shall display motor temperature status on the MMI screens and update the display if motors begin to overheat during operation.
The system shall enter a safe mode automatically if the operator inputs a movement command that exceeds the system's mechanical or software capabilities.
The system shall have both soft stops in software and hard stops in hardware to prevent movement beyond safe mechanical limits.
The system shall support pre-programmed movements for repeatable tasks such as moving between tool change positions or following an established path.
The system shall allow the operator to take manual control from a pre-programmed sequence at any point, especially during high-risk or precision tasks.
The system shall provide a ghost mode that visually predicts and displays the end position of a movement before execution to allow operator verification.
The system shall support fixed camera views in addition to variable viewpoints to maintain consistent spatial reference during operation.
The system shall provide variable camera viewpoints to improve depth perception and situational awareness during teleoperation.
The system shall provide augmented reality overlays on the display to guide alignment and positioning, especially for new or complex tasks.
The system shall provide high-resolution video feeds to support precision tasks such as electrical connector mating or screw alignment.
The system shall prioritize image resolution over frame rate for teleoperation, as tasks are performed slowly and require visual clarity.
The system shall provide force feedback to the operator to indicate resistance or obstruction during movement.
The system shall implement configurable no-go zones to prevent movement into areas where damage could occur to equipment or infrastructure.
The system shall provide audible alarms when the operator attempts to move into a defined no-go zone to prevent accidental damage.
The system shall have minimal latency between operator input and robotic response to support dexterous teleoperation.
The system shall support simulation of the entire operational environment to plan for worst-case scenarios and ensure task predictability.
The system shall incorporate computer vision to recognize and classify materials such as aluminium, rubber, and painted surfaces.
The system shall use material recognition data to inform no-go zones or gripping instructions based on surface type or object identity.
The system shall be adaptable to customer requirements with variants supporting longer arms, higher lifting capacity, or waterproofing while maintaining a common baseline design.
The system shall use robust wrist-mounted cameras for improved visibility during tasks.
